turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean water, mainly caused by the Moon’s gravity pulling on Earth’s oceans. The Sun also affects tides, but less strongly because it is much farther away. As Earth rotates, different coastlines move through areas of higher and lower water levels. Most places experience two high tides and two low tides each day, though patterns vary. Tides influence coastal ecosystems, navigation, fishing, and shoreline processes. Their timing depends on location, the Moon’s phase, and local geography. Understanding tides helps people predict ocean changes.
